title: An Introduction to Hodge Theory on Compact Orientable Surfaces with Boundary
content: This note is a sequel to a previous exposition of Hodge theory, aiming to provide a non-mathematician-friendly introduction to Hodge theory on surfaces with boundary. The main results include five versions of the Helmholtz-Hodge decompositions. The note also discusses the finite-dimensional spaces of harmonic vector fields with boundary conditions, whose dimensionalities equal the first Betti number of the underlying surface. Finally, the Helmholtz-Hodge decompositions are used to solve differential equations on surfaces.
